convoLines.text: "Oh! Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
Nods slowly. "Columbus, Ohio. I'll remember that. Everybody's from somewhere that isn't here."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Me? Buenos Aires, Argentina. I still dream in its weather — rain on a tin roof, that specific smell. I wake up here and for a second I'm furious at the sky for the swap."
"Still on where you're from."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Give it time."
"Vanessa owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
You show them American Hazelnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I save the best bite for last. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Nobody says Vanessa's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Did you leave someone behind? ...Sorry. You don't have to answer that."
Just: "Yeah." A long quiet. "Me too."
"I don't talk about that. Not because it's secret — because saying it out loud makes it real in a way I can't afford yet. Someday. Not today."
"Still on who you left behind."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Worth considering."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Vanessa always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Sleep's gone strange. I check everyone's shoes for wear at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"The fire feels smaller without Vanessa. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
You show them American Hazelnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — I've been turning something over. What do YOU think actually happened to us?"
"That's where I keep landing too. The question is what it wants. That's the truth of it."
Their friendliness thins — still there, just held at arm's length.
"Still on what you think happened to us."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Mark my words."
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Vanessa is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
You show them Common Plantain — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"...Actually, forget it."
"About that question — Have you ever hurt someone? Since all this started."
They nod, slow. "Okay. Thank you for telling me. That couldn't have been easy to say."
The ease drains out of it, a little.
"Still on whether you've hurt someone."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "I dreamed Vanessa was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"I asked Hugo about that question — Hugo's gone. What's the kindest thing someone's done for you out here?"
"That's the good stuff. Quiet generosity. It's holding this whole thing together."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on the kindest thing someone's done for you."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Since Hugo died... I keep expecting to see Hugo at the fire. Stupid."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
«مرحباً! ما اسمك؟»
«اتفقنا.» They nod back, slowly.
«شكراً. حقاً، شكراً.» (you catch 'شكراً' — thanks) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«لن أنسى هذا.» You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic. "Food?"
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «وين ننام هنا؟» (you catch 'ننام' — we sleep, 'وين' — where)
Doha laughs — with you, mostly. "Good try! Again — هذا صحيح.." They walk you through it, patient as sunrise.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You told me about people sharing food they couldn't spare. Quiet. No performance. Seen it again since?"
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
Megan shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took you — The Moot, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
«هيه... تتكلم عربي؟ لا؟ ...تباً.» (you catch 'عربي' — Arabic, 'لا' — no) "Fuck you." — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
«هذا صحيح.» (This is right. — you're fairly sure) They nod back, slowly.
«أنت إنسان طيب.» (You are a kind person. — you're fairly sure) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«ما قصرت، الله يخليك.» (You've done plenty — God keep you. — you're fairly sure) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «عندك أكل؟» (Do you have food? — you're fairly sure)
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You told me yes, once. No details. I haven't forgotten. I just don't ask."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "The Quiet Room. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"We started on that personal stuff, then got onto what's been happening."
"What are you hoping for? Not the big stuff. The small thing."
"God, yes. That's the dream now. Eight hours of not being afraid."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
«ما هذا المكان؟ أين نحن؟» (What is this place? Where are we? — you're fairly sure)
«مضبوط، كلامك صحيح.» (Spot on, your words are true. — you're fairly sure) They nod back, slowly. "Hello?"
«شكراً. حقاً، شكراً.» (Thank you. Truly, thank you. — you're fairly sure) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«لن أنسى هذا.» (I won't forget this. — you're fairly sure) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «كم يوم صار لنا هنا؟» (How many days have we been here? — you're fairly sure)
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."

deathBeat: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Vanessa Koffi is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: 🕯️ Vanessa Koffi is dead — a hushwolf. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Vanessa — and Vanessa is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
recoverHome: d42: That night, they bring Vanessa home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
vouch: d41: At the grave, Megan, Doha, Sigrun and 2 more speak for Hugo — "Vanessa trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
